source.title: Fine-Grained Manipulation of Arithmetic Neurons
source.authors: Wen-Yu Du; Rui Zheng; Tongxu Luo; Stephen Chung; Jie Fu

page_placements.theme: Small selected neuron sets causally control or predict specific behaviours beyond random controls

record.tranche_reason: The study uses arithmetic heuristic neurons as a tool for steering model outputs and reports how well its manipulation method performs. It does not test the listed claims about the share of interpretable neuron poles, explanation accuracy, attribution graphs, or canonical polysemantic examples.
record.gate_note: The paper reports causal neuron ablation and activation-editing results for arithmetic. These do not measure any listed version’s specific claim; the arithmetic manipulation findings are recorded as related but outside the listed versions. It also reports classifier accuracy for identifying heuristic classes, which evaluates its ranking method rather than the listed claims.
record.test_reason: The study uses activation patching and a linear classifier to rank arithmetic neurons, then steers Llama-3 addition outputs. It reports only how well its method localizes and manipulates neurons. It gives no share of neuron poles with one main job, no cross-model interpretability shares, no vision neurons, no attribution graphs and no simulation-based explanation scoring. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that ranking neurons by classifier weights enables fine-grained causal steering of addition outputs: over 80% for the ones place and nearly 70% for the tens place with K = 50. They attribute the effectiveness of top-ranked neurons to 'cleaner channels', which they support with SNR analysis.
record.recipe_differences: The paper ranks arithmetic neurons using a trained linear classifier and steers outputs by zeroing source neurons and shifting target neurons to activation centroids; it does not use the claim’s neuron-pole audit or attribution-graph method.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported manipulation varies by digit place, heuristic pair, neuron count, and model. The authors note poorer manipulation for some pairs, including pairs whose ones-place values differ substantially.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating 320 patching-selected arithmetic neurons cut Llama3-8B addition accuracy from 92.0% to 0.3%; ablating random neurons left it at 92.1% (±0.5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A small localized neuron set is causally necessary for addition in Llama3-8B.

fits_no_version.finding: Editing the top-50 heuristic neurons steered addition outputs to a target digit in 81.4% of cases (ones place) and 68.1% (tens place) for Llama3-8B. Rates were lower for Llama3.2-3B (49.4%) and Llama3-70B (42.3%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Targeted activation edits to ranked arithmetic heuristic neurons can steer addition outputs; effectiveness varies by digit place and model.

fits_no_version.finding: Classifying neurons by their maximally activating prompts (the Nikankin et al. method) assigned only 20% (66 of 320) of arithmetic neurons to any defined heuristic. The authors call this an incomplete understanding.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Max-activating-example labelling leaves most causally important arithmetic neurons without a heuristic label. This relates to, but does not measure, V6.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 8th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
record.problems: The paper says manipulation is not perfect and suggests superposition may contribute. Its analysis is limited to arithmetic prompts whose numbers are single tokens; it notes that results may differ for models with single-digit tokenization. The reported uncertainty is limited to the random-ablation control; uncertainty for manipulation rates is not stated.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed source-to-target pair rates in Tables 1–6 are not separately extracted; the rows record the aggregate rates reported for the ones and tens places and the additional-model table summaries. These steering outcomes do not test any listed claim version.

untested.parts: No audit of neuron-pole job shares in Qwen3-32B or any model.
No interpretability shares across models or scale; the three Llama-3 models are compared only on steering rates.
No InceptionV1 or vision polysemantic neuron analysis.
No comparison of architecture, regularization or tools as causes of interpretability shares.
No attribution graphs built from neurons, and no reconstruction-error comparison.
No test of whether explanations drawn from activating examples predict where held-out neurons fire.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

missing.what: Max-activation classification labels only 20% (66/320) of arithmetic neurons with a heuristic; this is related to V6 but does not measure it.
missing.locator: Section 4, 'Classification via Absolute Maximum Activation Value Misses 80% of the Neurons'

record.verdict_notes: The paper attributes imperfect manipulation, and off-target accuracy drops, to superposition, but gives no test of that. The 20% max-activation labelling result is the nearest thing to the claim's concerns, but it concerns heuristic labelling of a causally selected subset, not neuron-pole job shares. It does not count as a test of V1 or V6.

versions.untested_parts: Does not estimate the share of neuron poles with one or multiple main jobs, or the share not understood.
Tests manipulation in multiple Llama models, not whether the stated interpretability shares hold across models or scale.
Does not analyze InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose, recursive generalization, or superposition as an explanation of those examples.
Does not compare architecture, regularization, or tool quality as causes of interpretability shares, or estimate the stated vision-model shares.
Does not build attribution graphs or measure their explanatory coverage or reconstruction error.
Does not test whether explanations fit activating examples but fail to predict new activations.
Does not score neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: Llama3-8B
rows.stage_stated: pre-trained; not fine-tuned on arithmetic prompts
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed the activations of the 320 identified arithmetic neurons and evaluated arithmetic accuracy.
rows.note: The authors describe this as a catastrophic degradation; the result bears on causal arithmetic-neuron manipulation, not the listed versions.

rows.subject: Llama3-8B
rows.stage_stated: pre-trained; not fine-tuned on arithmetic prompts
rows.operation_detail: Masked 320 randomly selected neurons; result is averaged over three random seeds.
rows.note: Random-ablation control; accuracy is reported as maintained.

rows.subject: Llama3-8B
rows.stage_stated: pre-trained; not fine-tuned on arithmetic prompts
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed top-50 source-heuristic neurons and shifted top-50 target-heuristic neurons to the target heuristic’s mean activation.
rows.note: The paper reports this as the average manipulation rate for the ones place.
rows.check: Method-performance (steering) row; no version link. No baseline is stated in the source.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Treats single MLP neurons as meaningful units (heuristic neurons) and uses them to steer outputs. Does not test any claim version.

tranche.reason: Uses activation patching to pick 320 arithmetic neurons, then a linear classifier to rank them for steering addition outputs. It reports only how well its own method localizes and manipulates them. It gives no share of neurons with one main job and no test of any version.

source_check.notes: The ablation rows (Llama3-8B, 320 neurons, layers 16-31) only validate the paper's own localization and bear on no version. The number of evaluation prompts for the ablation is not stated. Possibly relevant but fitting no version: Section 4 says max-activation labelling assigns a heuristic to only 20% (66/320) of arithmetic neurons, and Appendix E shows 'noise channel' neurons.
